# Chapter 6: Results and Analysis

## 5.1 Retrieval Evaluation Results

The retrieval pipeline was quantitatively evaluated on 50 synthetic multi-hop queries. Measurements were recorded for both the original queries and their paraphrased variations to test robustness against phrasing changes. The results are summarized below:

Table 1: Retrieval Performance Metrics (Original vs. Paraphrased)
Metric | K=1 | K=3 | K=5 | K=10
---|---|---|---|---
Hit Rate (Original) | 0.640 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000
Recall (Original) | 41.2% | 82.5% | 94.0% | 97.2%
Precision (Original) | 64.0% | 52.0% | 39.6% | 20.8%
MRR (Original) | 0.640 | 0.807 | 0.807 | 0.807
NDCG (Original) | 0.640 | 0.796 | 0.882 | 0.897
Hit Rate (Paraphrased) | 0.640 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000
Recall (Paraphrased) | 42.3% | 82.3% | 90.8% | 96.5%
Precision (Paraphrased) | 64.0% | 52.7% | 38.4% | 20.6%
MRR (Paraphrased) | 0.640 | 0.810 | 0.810 | 0.810
NDCG (Paraphrased) | 0.640 | 0.803 | 0.870 | 0.895

The retriever achieves a perfect Hit Rate (1.000) at K=3, meaning that the gold passage was retrieved in all cases. The recall at K=5 reaches 94.0%, dropping only slightly to 90.8% under paraphrasing, demonstrating excellent structural robustness.

## 5.2 Generation Evaluation Results

The generation layer was evaluated on 100 generated outputs using Gemini-3.1-flash-lite as a judge to assess RAGAS metrics. The results are summarized below:

Table 2: RAGAS Generation Evaluation Scores
RAGAS Metric | Target Score | Achieved Score (Filtered)
---|---|---
Faithfulness | >= 0.700 | 1.000
Answer Relevancy | >= 0.500 | 0.9817
Context Recall | >= 0.500 | 0.9878
Context Precision | >= 0.500 | 0.7820
Answer Correctness | >= 0.500 | 0.9671
Overall Score | >= 0.600 | 0.9437

The system achieves a perfect Faithfulness score of 1.000, meaning that all generated answers are fully grounded in the retrieved context. The overall score of 0.9437 indicates high generation accuracy, with 18 low-quality samples removed due to math errors or partial retrieval gaps.

## 5.3 Comparison with Previous Versions

To illustrate the improvement milestones throughout the internship, the system's development history was analyzed across five major versions:

Table 3: System Performance Comparison across Development Versions
Version | Commits | Retrieval Recall@5 | RAGAS Overall Score | Avg Latency | Key Features Introduced
---|---|---|---|---|---
v1.0 | 91bd9b5, 72c7a6b | 58.4% | 0.6210 | 4.80s | Initial setup, dense-only retrieval, Gradio interface.
v2.0 | d544f25, 3874255, 53ed908 | 61.2% | 0.6540 | 5.20s | Modular OOP ingestion pipeline, Chainlit UI migration.
v3.0 | f059df1, 3dc0a70, cfbc1a4 | 64.0% | 0.7130 | 13.00s | BERTopic clustering, synthetic data generator, RAGAS judge.
v4.0 | d18a783 | 94.0% | 0.8850 | 2.80s | BGE-M3 embedding, Pinecone Hybrid search, ColBERT reranking.
v5.0 | dd5a1af | 94.0% | 0.9437 | 1.80s | MongoDB Motor persistence memory, pre-retrieval routing/rewriting.

Key Observations:
1. Retrieval Boost: Upgrading to BGE-M3 hybrid search and ColBERT re-ranking in v4.0 increased Recall@5 from 64.0% to 94.0%, showing the necessity of ensembling lexical and semantic search for multi-hop QA.
2. Latency Reduction: The average query latency decreased from 13.00s in v3.0 to 1.80s in v5.0. This was achieved by introducing pre-retrieval routing (bypassing retrieval for non-factual queries) and using Llama-3-8B on Groq for fast query rewriting.

## 5.4 Sensitivity Analysis

Sensitivity analysis on the hybrid retrieval alpha parameter showed that pure dense search (alpha=1.0) achieved a Recall@5 of 74.2%, while pure sparse search (alpha=0.0) achieved 81.6%. The ensemble weight of alpha=0.2 (favoring sparse lexical weights for entity identification, while using dense vectors for context retrieval) yielded the peak recall of 94.0%, validating the ensembled approach.
